feature.label: PLS HTMT and HTMT+ Discriminant Validity

claim.supported_scope: Deterministic pairwise original signed HTMT and HTMT+ for reflective constructs with at least two indicators, using Pearson correlations from the same model-wide complete cases and typed applicability states. Complete ordinary PLS bootstrapping also reports separately versioned BC Type-7 one-tailed upper alpha .05 inference with the documented .90 upper-bound decision and exact replicate bookkeeping.
claim.estimand: Original signed HTMT under henseler_et_al_htmt_v1 and absolute-correlation HTMT+ under the primary ringle_et_al_htmt_plus_v1 identity for each supported construct pair; complete-bootstrap inference asks whether the 90% bias-corrected upper bound is strictly below .90.
assumptions: Construct pairs are reflective, contain at least two indicators each, and use finite model-wide complete cases.
Pearson correlations and monotrait/heterotrait arithmetic means follow the frozen PLS_HTMT_V1 definition and deterministic recipe order.
The result persists both exact method versions, construct order, sign policy, symmetric typed cells, and unavailable reasons.
exclusions: Formative and single-indicator pairs, geometric-mean HTMT2+, clamping HTMT+ at one, and configurable two-tailed HTMT inference are excluded.
HTMT does not establish reliability, convergent validity, causal validity, or overall model fit.
Legacy assessment v2-v5 matrices cannot be relabeled as either current exact method.
warnings: The documented .90 bootstrap-inference decision is reported explicitly; researchers must separately justify any stricter context-specific criterion.
A nonpositive original signed monotrait mean or zero HTMT+ monotrait denominator makes the affected cell explicitly unavailable.

references.citation: Henseler, Ringle, and Sarstedt (2015), A New Criterion for Assessing Discriminant Validity in Variance-Based SEM, DOI 10.1007/s11747-014-0403-8
Ringle et al. (2023), A Perspective on Using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling in Data Articles, Appendix HTMT+, DOI 10.1016/j.dib.2023.109074
Independent Python original HTMT and HTMT+ reference
Independent NumPy/SciPy HTMT and bias-corrected Type-7 reference
SmartPLS Discriminant Validity Assessment and HTMT documentation, captured 2026-08-14

simulations.design: Reflective construct pairs across positive/mixed-sign correlations, two-item minima, near-zero denominators, discriminant-validity failure, and construct/indicator permutations.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen covariance scenarios and indexed data-generation seeds with deterministic calculation.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Every available value must match the independent reference within 1e-6, all typed unavailable states must be exact, and HTMT+ sign-reversal invariance must hold.

simulations.design: Formative blocks, single indicators, zero/nonpositive monotrait denominators, non-finite correlations, and values above one.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Unsupported or invalid cells must have the exact reason, valid values above one must remain unclamped, and non-finite input must fail explicitly.

boundaries.case: HTMT+ has a zero effective absolute monotrait mean or original HTMT has a nonpositive signed monotrait mean.
boundaries.expected_behavior: The affected cell is typed unavailable with the exact method-specific reason and no fabricated zero.

boundaries.case: Either construct is formative or contains fewer than two indicators.
boundaries.expected_behavior: The cell is explicitly not applicable and no HTMT value is emitted.

boundaries.case: One indicator is multiplied by negative one.
boundaries.expected_behavior: HTMT+ remains invariant; original signed HTMT changes or becomes unavailable according to its signed definition.

boundaries.case: The same complete cases, recipe order, and definitions execute repeatedly.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Method identities, typed cells, values, reasons, and warnings are exactly equal.

boundaries.case: A method version, construct order, sign flag, cell value/status/reason, symmetry, or denominator state is changed.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict project validation rejects the archive.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject an archive whose identity differs from PLS HTMT/HTMT+ assessment.
Reject a payload with missing, swapped, or unknown original/plus method versions.
Reject matrices whose complete-case dataset fingerprint differs.
Reject an archive entry whose assessment or matrix checksum differs.
Reject duplicate keys, unknown fields, non-finite values, asymmetric cells, invalid diagonals, or inconsistent status/reason pairs.
Never reinterpret assessment v2-v5 absolute matrices as current signed HTMT or exact HTMT+ evidence.

persistence.legacy_policy: Legacy v2-v5 matrices remain readable under their historical identity and cannot carry either current exact method version.

native.gui_cli_parity_rule: GUI and CLI must produce the same exact method versions, construct order, typed cells, values, unavailable reasons, one-tailed decisions, and replicate accounting for identical inputs.
accessibility_rules: Each heatmap has an equivalent accessible matrix table.
Values, threshold direction, unavailable reasons, and warnings are not conveyed by color alone.
